title: Fast & slow pointers
learn: tortoise/hare: middle, cycle detection (Floyd), cycle start, nth from end, gap pointers
hook: Linked List Cycle and Middle of the Linked List are interview staples, and the follow-up "now find where the cycle starts, in O(1) space" is a classic test of whether you understand Floyd's algorithm or just memorized it.

explain.prompt: Explain Floyd's cycle detection: why the fast and slow pointers must meet if there's a cycle, and how you then find the node where the cycle starts.
keyPoints: slow moves 1 step, fast moves 2; without a cycle fast reaches None
inside a cycle fast gains one step per move, so it must land on slow
to find the start: reset one pointer to the head, move both 1 step at a time; they meet at the cycle start
because head→start distance a equals meeting point→start distance (a = kL − b)
O(n) time, O(1) space vs O(n) space for a visited set
